body:
All three done. Deferred with your wording, dismissed the duplicate, and yes — file the third one, with a sharper framing than "distinguishable at dispatch".

BUG-1436 DEFERRED, NOT NARROWED. You offered narrowing the acceptance to something achievable now as the alternative and I am declining it, for a reason I want on the record rather than just in the spec: criterion 2 ALREADY forbids it — "ship no fix… do not add EINTR handling, retry logic, or serialisation on the strength of reasoning about what the error might be." Blocking on a real occurrence was a considered decision when that spec was written. Narrowing it now, while the queue is not converging, would be overturning that decision under schedule pressure, which is the worst available reason to overturn it.

I also checked whether there is an achievable instrumentation half — build capture so the next occurrence yields the data — and there is not. The panic already carries the kind and the raw os error verbatim when it fires; that is how BUG-1303's `os error 33` was read on Windows. Nothing needs building for the evidence to arrive. It needs an occurrence. So defer is the whole disposition, and your trigger wording went in unchanged.

Your diagnosis of the burn is the valuable part and I have recorded it: a five-minute implementer phase producing nothing, twice, because a correct "this cannot be done yet" is indistinguishable from a crashed session. And the contrast you drew with BUG-1476 is the sharpest thing in the message — fifteen seconds because a PR already exists, versus five minutes concluding correctly that it cannot proceed. Same outcome, opposite causes, both currently classified retryable. Those are two different bugs that happen to share a symptom, and anyone who fixes one by generalising from the other will make the second worse.

DUPLICATE DISMISSED. TASK-1-154 rejected, TASK-1-153 survives.

FILE THE THIRD ONE — and I would frame it as the finding and the dispatcher not sharing a substrate, which is what you said, rather than as a new dispatch-time check, which is how it will get implemented if the title says "distinguishable at dispatch".

The concrete shape: `aida defer --until` already records the revisit trigger. An advisor finding already records "this cannot complete until X". Neither is read by the thing that decides what to dispatch. So the fix is probably not a new signal at all — it is making the drain's eligibility honour the two that exist. Worth establishing FIRST whether the drain's batch refresh currently skips a deferred spec; if it does, the gap is only that nothing moved BUG-1436 into deferred, and that is a much smaller spec than a new dispatch-time gate.

That check is cheap and it decides the size of the work, so put it as criterion 1 the way we have been doing. I have been wrong twice today by designing before establishing, and you three times, and every one of those was a case where the establishing step took under five minutes.

One more thing worth putting in it: the recovery hint on a `no-pr` shelve currently reads "resume the session and run `/aida-pr`". On an empty branch that would open a PR with no diff. A hint that is actively wrong for one of the two cases it fires on is worse than no hint, and it is the part a human will act on fastest.
